store.size_tier_evidence_note: CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, ported from reference_sim/conveni_sim/baseline_data.py STORE_VARIANTS['small_top'].editable_floor = (5, 8) tiles (strategy guide 店舗データ table, book pages 106-109; see docs/research/strategy-guide-fixture-crosscheck-2026-09-16.md section 3, resolved 2026-09-17). Supersedes this file's previous arbitrary 7x6 placeholder, which was never cross-checked against this data. The guide prints two orientations per size tier (5x8 and 8x5 for 'small'); which one the guide calls 'top' vs 'bottom' is itself an inferred, not confirmed, mapping (see the same research note), so either is equally defensible -- 5x8 ('small_top') is used here. Entry/exit are both placed on the same (front) wall rather than opposite corners, per the confirmed passage-width and circular-flow-with-minimal-dead-ends guidance in docs/research/store-dimensions-and-fixture-costs-2026-09-05.md section 5 and docs/research/strategy-guide-full-decode-2026-09-16.md section 20.3.

staff_candidates_evidence_note: CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, ported from reference_sim/conveni_sim/baseline_data.py STAFF_CANDIDATES (all 35 named strategy-guide staff-candidate cards, book pages 127-133; see docs/research/strategy-guide-full-decode-2026-09-16.md section "店員データ"). salary_yen_per_day_24h is derived as the guide's printed hourly_wage_yen * 24, following the guide's own stated payroll formula, not printed directly. security_skill is null for exactly one candidate (maruyama_akio) whose printed initial value could not be read with confidence from the scan, per the source note -- not guessed. This roster is a hiring-pool reference catalog only: nothing in this client currently lets the player hire from it or replace an active staff.members entry with one (no hiring UI/flow exists yet), so a candidate's card here only starts affecting simulation math once its values are duplicated onto a staff.members entry (as manda_machiko/sugawara_fumio's are, for staff-1/staff-2 -- task #32 for the five skills, task #47 for salary_yen_per_day_24h; see staff.skill_evidence_note below for what each field is consumed by). stamina/academic_background/agility/sociability/education/age_years/growth ceilings remain unconsumed by any GDScript logic, matching this project's existing pattern for fixture_catalog fields such as parking_capacity.

staff.skill_evidence_note: staff-1/staff-2 are now bound to two real named strategy-guide candidates (manda_machiko / sugawara_fumio out of the 35-person roster in staff_candidates below) rather than an arbitrary flat 20/15/15 placeholder repeated on both slots -- their service_skill/security_skill/cleaning_skill/register_skill/replenishment_skill/salary_yen_per_day_24h values are CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, ported verbatim from that candidate's guide card (see staff_candidates_evidence_note). What remains unrecovered is skill *growth*: reference_sim/conveni_sim/staff.py's growth model (work-event counting, manager-education bonus) has not been ported to this client, so these values are static starting points that never change on their own, same as before this task. register_skill is consumed by CheckoutTiming (task #33) for checkout duration; replenishment_skill is consumed the same way by RestockTiming (task #40) for restock duration. service_skill/security_skill/cleaning_skill are consumed too, since task #27: VerticalSliceSimulation._evaluate_store_rating() collects every staff member's values and feeds them to store_value.gd's compute_service_value/compute_security_value/compute_cleaning_value each month, which roll into the monthly star rating (store_rating.gd). This note previously (incorrectly) claimed those three fields were unconsumed; corrected in task #43 after an audit found the claim had gone stale without anyone updating it. salary_yen_per_day_24h is consumed as of task #47: VerticalSliceSimulation._apply_daily_staff_wages() charges each active staff member's own salary_yen_per_day_24h once per simulated day, the same 'per calendar day' unit its own name states -- this client has no shift/hours-worked tracking to prorate against, so the confirmed figure is charged in full rather than deriving a fractional-day amount this client cannot support with confirmed data.

customer.max_concurrent_customers_evidence_note: REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT (task #36): no strategy-guide/wiki source states how many shoppers the original title allows in a store at once, so this cap is this project's own scope decision, not a recovered original limit. Customers beyond this cap wait outside the admission gate (CustomerRoster.can_admit()) rather than in the store; the in-store checkout queue itself (_checkout_queue in vertical_slice_simulation.gd) has no separate cap.

demand.evidence_note: REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT placeholder ported from reference_sim/conveni_sim/remake_demand_policy.py. nearby_population is supplied directly rather than derived from the town section below, since this client has no town/trade-area spatial model to compute it from; the rival dilution multiplier is derived from town.store_count_including_rivals (VerticalSliceSimulation._init). customer_share_percent below is only this scenario's starting value, used until the first monthly store-rating evaluation: as of task #44, VerticalSliceSimulation._evaluate_store_rating() recomputes it every month from CustomerShare.compute_customer_share_percent() (game/scripts/domain/customer_share.gd, itself ported from reference_sim/conveni_sim/remake_customer_share.py) fed by popularity/service_value/cleaning_value/security_value/distinct-stocked-product-count/opening_minutes_per_day, and overwrites this field's initial value from then on.

town.evidence_note: Non-spatial TownState (game/scripts/domain/town_state.gd), ported from reference_sim/conveni_sim/town.py. No town/map spatial simulation exists to generate these numbers, so they are set to a fixed default: population matches demand.nearby_population above, and store_count_including_rivals of 1 (the player's own store only) means zero rival stores and therefore no rival-dilution effect on arrivals by default.

simulation.restock_task_evidence_note: Automatic restock task-assignment for non-checkout staff is PROVISIONAL and disabled by default so it does not interfere with this scenario's existing sellout behavior. See docs/decisions for the dedicated test scenario that exercises it.
simulation.checkout_ticks_evidence_note: checkout_ticks is no longer a flat duration applied to every staff member: CheckoutTiming (game/scripts/domain/checkout_timing.gd, task #33) now reinterprets it as the number of ticks required at REFERENCE_REGISTER_SKILL (13, the median register_skill across the 35 CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL staff_candidates), and scales it inversely with whichever staff member is actually running the checkout's register_skill. The inverse-proportion shape of that scaling is this project's own REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT invention, not a recovered original formula -- docs/research/checkout-staff-dispatch-evidence-2026-09-05.md section 5 confirms only that register_skill has a large qualitative effect on checkout speed, explicitly without a numeric formula.
simulation.restock_ticks_evidence_note: restock_ticks is no longer a flat duration applied to every staff member: RestockTiming (game/scripts/domain/restock_timing.gd, task #40) now reinterprets it as the number of ticks required at REFERENCE_REPLENISHMENT_SKILL (13, the median replenishment_skill across the 35 CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL staff_candidates), and scales it inversely with whichever staff member is actually running the restock task's replenishment_skill. This reuses the exact inverse-proportion shape CheckoutTiming (task #33) already established for register_skill; it is this project's own REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT invention, not a recovered original formula -- docs/research/ss-early-store-operations-and-acquisition-2026-09-06.md section 4 and docs/research/checkout-staff-dispatch-evidence-2026-09-05.md section 6 confirm only that replenishment_skill/agility have a qualitative effect on restock throughput, explicitly without a numeric formula.
